criterion: render-research NEXT.md item 1 (2026-10-22): surface-stable fractal dithering for the dither and palette lighting layer. Target: temporal instability on a camera orbit at least 50% below the current screen-space dither with the paired bootstrap interval excluding zero; at most 0.3 ms at 1080p by GPU timestamps; CPU and GPU parity within the repo ditherlight tolerances on WARP and lavapipe; controls that must fail.
written: 2026-10-22, before any code and before any run
overlap_check: Branches and PRs touching dither were read first. Nothing implements surface-stable or fractal dithering. Related and reused: ditherlight (PR 144, raw/renderer/style_ditherlight.hpp) whose Anchor enum has Screen, WorldFixed and WorldOctave; project-docs/DITHER-LIGHTING-RESULTS.md (world anchors cut surface-lock error L but cost tone accuracy A, 8 to 15 against 2.4); project-docs/NOVELTY.md (records Dither3D as KNOWN and says the octave snap has seams the fractal construction avoids). PR 197 (P8b) is the offline dither module and is untouched. The P8 GPU stage (feat/p8-noise-gpu) is noise only. This work adds Anchor::Fractal to the existing ditherlight pass and duplicates none of them. PR 209 (art_scene, art_metrics) is not merged, so this branch carries its own small scene and metric helpers under the fractal_ prefix; they should be folded into art_metrics after 209 lands.
source: Surface-Stable Fractal Dithering, Rune Skovbo Johansen (Runevision), 2025, runevision.com/tech/dither3d; repository github.com/runevision/Dither3D, MPL-2.0. Only the published description is used (dots stick to the surface; on-screen dot size and spacing stay near constant; dots may be added but not removed as a pattern grows on screen, removed but not added as it shrinks). No code was read or copied. The construction below is derived here.

design.chart: The existing triplanar anchor chart of ditherlight (dominant axis of the anchor normal on the anchor position).
design.level: Footprint s = pa * depth (world size of a pixel). Target cell S = px * s. Continuous level lambda = log2(S / cell). n0 = floor(lambda), m = 1 - frac(lambda). Fine cell size cell * 2^n0 (on screen between px/2 and px pixels), coarse cell size twice that. Integer cell indices i, j at the fine size; the coarse index is (i >> 1, j >> 1), so coarse cells are exact unions of fine cells.
design.threshold: Fractal Bayer: rank_K(x, y) = sum over k < K of digit(x_k, y_k) 4^(K-1-k), digit = ((x_k xor y_k) << 1) | y_k, K = 6 (equals bayer8Rank at K = 3). T = (rank + 0.5) / 4^K. With Tc from the coarse cell and Tf from the fine cell, Tf is approximately (d + Tc) / 4 with d the fine sub-cell leading digit, so a coarse-lit cell keeps its corner sub-cell lit at the finer level (dots are added, not removed, when the pattern grows).
design.blend: B = (1 - m) Tc + m Tf, then T_m = G_m(B) with G_m(B) = 1/4 * sum over d in 0..3 of clamp((B - m d / 4) / (1 - 3 m / 4), 0, 1), the marginal CDF of B. T_m is uniform for every m (the pattern keeps its mean tone), equals the coarse pattern at m = 0 and the fine pattern at m = 1, and is continuous in the level, so no dot pops at an octave boundary.
design.implementation: raw/renderer/style_ditherlight.hpp: Anchor::Fractal = 3 and fractalThreshold(), float64. GPU: the same branch in the style_ditherlight pass of style.wgsl (HLSL regenerated by wgsl_to_hlsl.py), f32, no new uniform fields (cell, px and pa already exist).
design.controls_in_code: DitherPlan::fractalDepth (<= 0 is off) fixes the depth in the scale term. A control only, like hemiConst.

metric.scene: An owned analytic courtyard ray cast in float64: ground plane, four walls 14 high at half-size 18, a plinth box, two spheres and a column; two radial lamps with shadow rays; low-frequency albedo. Sky pixels are excluded from every metric (no surface to anchor).
metric.orbit: target (0, 1, 0), radius 8.5, eye height 4.2, azimuth from 20 degrees in 1 degree steps, vertical field of view 0.75 rad, 48 frames at 320 x 180.
metric.presets: ink (1 bit) and tones4 (4 levels), Bayer-class threshold, px = 2, cell = 0.1.
metric.temporal_instability: the rr-bounds definition (evidence/rr-bounds.json): mean over valid pixels and colour channels of |(out_t - warp(out_t-1)) - (ref_t - warp(ref_t-1))| on 8-bit display codes divided by 255, nearest-pixel warp by the true motion vector; history is valid where the reprojected pixel is inside the frame, shows the same object, and its depth agrees within 2%. out is the dithered frame; ref is the undithered tone through the same ink and paper mix and sRGB encoding. Frames 1 to 47.
metric.bootstrap: paired over frames, 10,000 resamples, a fixed seed recorded; 95% interval of mean(fractal - screen) and of 1 - mean(fractal) / mean(screen).

f1_temporal.what: Fractal against Anchor::Screen with the same preset, threshold family and tone, per preset
f1_temporal.bound: point estimate of the relative reduction at least 0.50 for both presets
f1_temporal.kill: the paired 95% interval of mean(fractal - screen) contains zero for ink: the technique is dropped from this layer
f1_temporal.prediction: holds for ink at 0.6 to 0.85, moderate confidence. tones4 flips are smaller steps; I expect 0.5 to 0.8 and the bound could miss.

f2_controls.what: (a) Screen against Screen as the candidate; (b) the fractal pattern with the anchor positions taken from frame (7 t mod 48) instead of frame t; (c) the scale term broken: fractalDepth fixed at the orbit radius
f2_controls.bound: (a) and (b) reduction below 0.50 on ink; (c) fails f1 on ink or fails f3
f2_controls.prediction: (a) 0 exactly; (b) near or below zero; (c) fails f3 and probably f1

f3_scale_invariance.what: A fronto-parallel plane of constant tone 0.5 at depths 4, 5.7, 8, 11.3, 16 (a 4x range), 320 x 180, ink preset: horizontal level-change density per adjacent pixel pair
f3_scale_invariance.bound: max over depths / min over depths at most 1.5
f3_scale_invariance.prediction: about 1.1 to 1.3; the broken scale term gives well above 3

f4_structure.what: unit tests: rank_K at K = 3 equals bayer8Rank; T_m equals the coarse threshold at m = 0 and the fine at m = 1; T_m is uniform (16 bins each within 3% of 1/16 on a 512 x 512 chart) at m = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75; at m = 1 every coarse-lit cell has its corner sub-cell lit

f5_gpu_parity.what: the style_ditherlight pass with anchor 3 against the float64 reference on D3D12 WARP and Vulkan lavapipe (CI) and the RTX 4090 locally, on orbit frames 0 and 24 at 256 x 144, both presets
f5_gpu_parity.bound: the repo ditherlight GPU bound from evidence/cpp-port-style-bounds.json: level mismatch fraction at most 0.0005, over-2-codes fraction at most 0.0005, mean absolute code at most 0.12. Built-in control: the reference with the chart shifted one cell must exceed the mismatch bound.
f5_gpu_parity.prediction: holds; cell-edge flips from f32 floor(u / size) are about 1e-4 of pixels

f6_cost.what: RTX 4090, D3D12, 1920 x 1080, frame 0 of the orbit: GPU timestamps (the PR 204 interface) around 10 back-to-back dispatches of the style_ditherlight pass in one submission, median of 21 submissions, per-dispatch time; anchor 3 and anchor 0 interleaved; under the shared GPU lock
f6_cost.bound: extra time of anchor 3 over anchor 0 at most 0.3 ms. The whole-pass time is recorded and not gated; if it exceeds 0.3 ms the PR says so.
f6_cost.prediction: extra under 0.05 ms (ALU only); whole pass about 0.2 to 0.4 ms (96 bytes a pixel read)

f7_goldens.what: tests/test_fractal_dither.cpp: FNV-1a over the level plane of orbit frame 0 at 256 x 144 for ink and tones4 with Anchor::Fractal
f7_goldens.bound: equal to the pinned record on GCC and MSVC
f7_goldens.prediction: holds on both; a difference is recorded per compiler family

f8_accuracy.what: recorded, not gated: tone accuracy A of the 2026-10-15 protocol (100 x mean |cbrt(box4 out) - cbrt(box4 tone)|, 4 x 4 box, linear light) for screen, world-octave and fractal on the orbit
f8_accuracy.prediction: fractal A between screen (about 2.4) and world-octave (about 14); the cost the 2026-10-15 results found for any surface-attached pattern

does_not_prove: Perception: the metric counts pixel changes, not viewer-visible swim, and the 2026-10-15 results show the metric favours whichever pattern moves less on screen. Moving objects (the chart is the anchor position the G-buffer supplies), grazing angles (the scale term uses depth only) or curved surfaces beyond the triplanar seams. The palette-lighting layer (style_palettelight) keeps its own screen Bayer lookups; this work wires ditherlight only. That the construction matches Dither3D's shader.
kill_rule: If the f1 kill fires, record it in evidence/fractal-dither-runs.json, keep the CPU reference behind its option, and stop.
